extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and aesthetics (readers of Kant)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository philosophical criteria for forming and evaluating pure aesthetical judgements about the Beautiful and the Sublime in nature, including their grounding, modalities (necessity, communicability), and relation to moral Ideas and imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of pleasurable judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: In reference to the feeling of pleasure an object is to be classified as either pleasant, or beautiful, or sublime, or good (absolutely) (jucundum, pulchrum, sublime, honestum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic taxonomy: pleasant (motive of desire), beautiful (pleasure in mere judgement), sublime (pleasure through opposition to sensible interest), and the absolutely good (moral). Use this classification as the starting point for any aesthetic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasant (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pleasant, as motive of desire, is always of one and the same kind...account is taken only of the number of its charms...this can be made intelligible only by quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasure of this sort is quantified (mass/quantity of sensation), belongs to mere enjoyment, and does not refer to culture or require conceptual reduction. Not relevant for pure aesthetical judgement of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Beautiful is what pleases in the mere judgement (and therefore not by the medium of sensation in accordance with a concept of the Understanding). It must please apart from all interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty requires a representation of a certain quality of the object that can be made intelligible and reduced to concepts (though not in the act of pure aesthetical judgement). It cultivates attention to purposiveness in the feeling of pleasure. When evaluating beauty, ensure the judgment is disinterested (no private/sensible interest) and that the pleasure arises from free play of faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sublime is what pleases immediately through its opposition to the interest of sense. It is an object (of nature) the representation of which determines the mind to think the unattainability of nature regarded as a presentation of Ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sublime judgments involve the Imagination strained toward Ideas (the supersensible). They are negative (pleasure arises by opposition to sensibility), often evoke astonishment bordering on terror, and call upon moral or intellectual capacities rather than mere sensory delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolutely good (moral) as distinct category
rubrics_metrics.description: The absolutely good, subjectively judged according to the feeling that it inspires (the Object of the moral feeling), is specially distinguished by the modality of a necessity that rests a priori upon concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not merely aesthetical but deterministic/practical: it involves a command for assent and is a determinant judgement tied to Freedom. When encountering claims of necessity in aesthetic contexts, distinguish moral/determinant judgments from pure reflective aesthetic judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic purposiveness (purposiveness without concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetical purposiveness is the conformity to law of the Judgement in its freedom. The satisfaction in the object depends on the relation in which we wish to place the Imagination; always provided that it by itself entertains the mind in free occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pure aesthetic judgement must not be determined by sensation or concepts; it is a subjective purposiveness (without an objective concept). Evaluate whether a judgement arises from this free purposiveness rather than from teleology, sensation, or concept-driven cognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness requirement for beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Beautiful must please apart from all interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true aesthetic judgement of beauty is disinterested: check that the pleasure is not grounded in desire, utility, or personal interest. If interest or concept influences the judgement, it is not a pure aesthetic judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative vs positive satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The satisfaction in the Sublime of nature is then only negative (whilst that in the Beautiful is positive); viz. a feeling that the Imagination is depriving itself of its freedom, while it is purposively determined according to a different law from that of its empirical employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distinguishing sublime from beautiful responses, note whether the pleasure is experienced as a negative contraction/limitation of sensibility (sublime) or as a positive play/expansion (beautiful).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime requires susceptibility to Ideas / moral feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: That the mind be attuned to feel the sublime postulates a susceptibility of the mind for Ideas...without development of moral Ideas...the sublime presents itself to the uneducated man merely as terrible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to judge the sublime presupposes cultural/moral development; when assessing whether an observer's judgement is valid, consider whether they possess the requisite moral/intellectual disposition to connect the sensible presentation to Ideas (the supersensible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicability and claim to universal validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the Beautiful and Sublime, as explanations of aesthetical universally valid judging, are referred to subjective grounds...they are referred to subjective grounds...they acquire an interest in reference to society (in which this communication is possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic judgements claim a kind of universal communicability (we expect others to agree). For beauty, this claim requires an a priori basis and a Deduction; for the sublime the claim is tied to shared moral susceptibility. Use communicability as a test of whether a judgement aspires to universal assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of an a priori principle / Deduction for validity
rubrics_metrics.description: In this modality of aesthetical judgements...it enables us to recognise in them an a priori principle...The claim of an aesthetical judgement to universal validity for every subject requires...a Deduction (or legitimatising of its pretensions) in addition to its Exposition; if it is concerned with satisfaction or dissatisfaction in the form of the Object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a taste-judgement claims necessity or universal validity, one must seek an a priori foundation (a Deduction). Kant argues this is required especially for judgements of the Beautiful in nature; evaluate whether such claims rest on communicable a priori principles rather than empirical agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction applies to Beauty in nature (not Sublime)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deduction of aesthetical judgements on the objects of nature must not be directed to what we call Sublime in nature, but only to the Beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat attempts to justify aesthetic judgments differently: seek systematic, a priori grounding (Deduction) for claims of beauty; sublime judgements, being tied to a mental state and moral Ideas, are explained rather than deduced in the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude teleological/conceptual determinations for pure judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Transcendental Aesthetic of Judgement we must speak solely of pure aesthetical judgements; consequently our examples are not to be taken from such beautiful or sublime objects of Nature as presuppose the concept of a purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging purely aesthetical qualities, avoid bringing in teleological or conceptual explanations (e.g., thinking of the ocean as a habitat or resource). Ensure the judgement refers to the immediate sensible presentation only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime: mathematical vs dynamical varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: This Idea of the supersensible...is awakened in us by means of an object, whose aesthetical appreciation strains the Imagination to its utmost bounds, whether of extension (mathematical) or of its might over the mind (dynamical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize two paths to the sublime: magnitude (mathematical) and power/threat (dynamical). Analyses should specify which mode is in play and how the imagination is strained toward Ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affect/emotion typology for aesthetic status
rubrics_metrics.description: Every affection of the strenuous kind...is aesthetically sublime, e.g. wrath, even despair...affections of the languid kind...have nothing noble in themselves, but they may be reckoned under the sensuously beautiful. Tender emotions, if they rise to affections, are worthless (sentimentality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating emotional content (in art, rhetoric, or experience), categorize affections: strenuous (can be sublime), languid (sensuously beautiful), or tender (sentimental/weak). Avoid conflating sentimental emotionalism with true sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic nobility and admiration vs astonishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Nobility: absence of affection in a mind that vigorously follows its unalterable principles is sublime...this is called noble...applied to things when they do not so much arouse astonishment...as admiration (astonishment that does not cease when the novelty disappears).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mere novelty-based astonishment from lasting admiration. The latter indicates a nobility (sublime) grounded in alignment with Ideas rather than transient surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enthusiasm vs fanaticism (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enthusiasm (Idea of the Good conjoined with affection) is called sublime...fanaticism is a delusion...a delusion that we can will ourselves to see something beyond all bounds of sensibility...fanaticism is comparable to monomania; the latter is least compatible with the sublime, because in its detail it is ridiculous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat enthusiasm as a potentially sublime transient state, but regard fanaticism as a pathology that undermines true sublimity. In evaluating expressions of religious or political fervor, beware of mistaking fanaticism for genuine sublime sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity (purposiveness without art) as style of the sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity (purposiveness without art) is as it were the style of Nature in the sublime, and so also of Morality which is a second (supersensible) nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value simplicity and unadorned purposiveness when assessing sublime expressions. Ornamental or overly-artful presentation can detract from the pure negative grandeur associated with the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social communicability and solitude as sublime (contextual criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation from all society is regarded as sublime, if it rests upon Ideas that overlook all sensible interest. To be sufficient for oneself, and consequently to have no need of society...is something bordering on the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the motivation for solitude: self-sufficiency grounded in Ideas (sublime) vs misanthropy/shyness (contemptible or hateful). Context and underlying principles matter in evaluating whether solitude is aesthetically sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical vs transcendental approaches (methodological criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: We can now compare the Transcendental Exposition of aesthetical judgements with the Physiological worked out by Burke...The empirical exposition may be a beginning...but a transcendental discussion...is an essential part of the Critique of Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate empirical/physiological accounts (e.g., Burke's) that locate aesthetic experience in bodily responses from transcendental accounts that seek a priori principles. Use the appropriate method depending on whether the aim is description (psychology) or justification (philosophy) of aesthetic claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination's role and schematism requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Imagination by the laws of Association makes our state of contentment dependent on physical causes; but it also...is the instrument of Reason and its Ideas...and as such has might to maintain our independence of natural influences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the imagination is operating merely associatively (sensory dependence) or as instrument of Reason (raising us to supersensible Ideas). True aesthetic judgement involves the latter free schematism rather than mere associative response.
